newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish bourse extends fall, rebound seen on Monday.
newsitem.headline: Polish bourse extends fall, rebound seen on Monday.

text.p: The Polish bourse fell for the fifth day running but analysts said a rise was likely on Monday with the market maintaining its slight downtrend during next week's offering of copper firm KGHM Polska Miedz.

"It seems there'll be a slight rebound on Monday but there doesn't have to be...it seems that overall there could still be slight falls over the next two months," said Remigiusz Tarka, an analyst at IB Austria Securities.
On Friday the Polish treasury set the institutional price of the issue of 55 million to 72 million shares at 19.5 zlotys, the retail price at 19 zlotys.
The main market's all-share WIG index fell 0.2 percent 15,147.7 points and turnover rose 15.3 percent to 115.9 million zlotys on both markets.
Analysts said a good sign was the rebounding of stocks suffering recent falls, such as Debica, which rose 6.3 percent on Friday with stronger buying after price fixing following Thursday's drop.
They said large Bank Handlowy could start trade on Monday over 40 zlotys after having sold at its privatisation offer at 35 zlotys.
